metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (Ruby on Rails controller) with an implied deployable entry point (Rails app server). Single-service application with database dependency (MySQL). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Orders controller with CRUD operations (create, show, index) backed by a MySQL database with write endpoints (order creation, payment charging). Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.18 yields Not Ready band but 11 High findings (< 12) maps to Remediation Required tier. The extremely low overall score reflects a system with no modernization investments across all categories; the count-based tier correctly identifies it as requiring systematic remediation rather than Not Ready (which requires ≥12 High findings).

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on raw EC2 instances with Mongrel app server behind Apache mod_proxy_balancer. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: No managed compute services in use. All compute is self-managed EC2 requiring manual patching, scaling, and capacity planning.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed container orchestration (ECS/Fargate) or serverless (Lambda) after the prerequisite Ruby/Rails version upgrade and containerization.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: MySQL 5.1 is self-managed on a separate EC2 instance. No managed database services (RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB) in use.
findings.gap: All databases self-managed on EC2 with manual patching, backup, and scaling responsibilities.
findings.recommendation: Migrate MySQL to Amazon RDS for MySQL or Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ deployment, automated backups, and managed patching.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: The order creation workflow (create order → charge payment) is entirely hardcoded in the controller with no orchestration service.
findings.gap: No workflow orchestration — business-critical multi-step operations (order + payment) are hardcoded in application code with no error recovery.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS Step Functions for the order-payment workflow to provide retry logic, error handling, and state management.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. Payment gateway call is a synchronous SOAP request blocking the HTTP request thread.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries — tight synchronous coupling to external payment gateway.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS or EventBridge for decoupling payment processing from order creation.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No IaC defines network configuration. No VPC, subnet, or security group configuration exists in the repository. No HTTPS termination.
findings.gap: No evidence of VPC, private subnets, security groups, or network segmentation. No HTTPS termination at the application tier.
findings.recommendation: Define network infrastructure in IaC with private subnets for application and database tiers, least-privilege security groups, and TLS termination.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront as entry point. Apache mod_proxy_balancer provides basic reverse proxying with no throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.gap: Services exposed through basic Apache reverse proxy with no managed entry point.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) or API Gateway as the entry point with TLS termination, throttling, and authentication.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. Deployment is to a fixed set of EC2 hosts — all capacity is statically provisioned.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity is statically provisioned with no ability to respond to traffic changes.
findings.recommendation: Implement auto-scaling via ECS service auto-scaling or EC2 Auto Scaling Groups with appropriate scaling policies.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration found. MySQL 5.1 on EC2 has no automated backup, no PITR, no retention policy defined.
findings.gap: No backup configuration for the database. Data loss event would result in unrecoverable data loss.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS with automated backups (7+ day retention) and PITR. Until migration, implement mysqldump-based backups to S3.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists in the repository. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any infrastructure definition files found. All infrastructure is manually created.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage — all infrastructure created manually (ClickOps). No reproducibility, no DR capability.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or AWS CDK: compute, database, networking, and operational resources.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Manual deployment via Capistrano 2 to a fixed set of EC2 hosts.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments are manual. No automated testing, building, or deployment stages.
findings.recommendation: Implement a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions or AWS CodePipeline) with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Ruby 1.8.7 with Rails 2.3 — both extremely end-of-life. AWS SDK for Ruby requires Ruby 2.x+ minimum.
findings.gap: Compound legacy — language version AND framework are both deeply EOL. Cannot use modern AWS SDK or gem ecosystem.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Ruby 3.2+ with Rails 7.x as a prerequisite to any cloud-native modernization.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries. Single Rails application handling orders, payments, and asset serving in one deployable unit.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with pervasive shared state. Cannot independently scale, deploy, or evolve components.
findings.recommendation: Decompose using Strangler Fig pattern — extract payment processing as the first independent service.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. Payment gateway SOAP call blocks the HTTP request thread. No async patterns.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous HTTP/SOAP. Payment charging blocks the order creation request.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async processing for payment operations using SQS. Return order confirmation immediately with pending payment status.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: The charge_card method makes a synchronous SOAP call to an external payment gateway that can exceed 30 seconds. No async job processing.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Payment gateway calls can timeout without graceful handling.
findings.recommendation: Implement async job processing for payment operations. Return 202 Accepted with a job ID; provide a status polling endpoint.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. Controller routes have no version prefix, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — any API changes break all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (/api/v1/) for new services extracted from the monolith.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: Payment gateway endpoint hardcoded in config/payment.yml. No service registry, no dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded in configuration files with no dynamic discovery.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for service endpoints. Adopt AWS Cloud Map for future microservices.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: No managed object storage. Static assets served directly from the Rails application with no S3, no CloudFront.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems served directly by the application. No S3 or managed storage.
findings.recommendation: Migrate static assets to S3 with CloudFront CDN distribution.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Direct SQL queries (find_by_sql with raw string interpolation) in controllers. No repository pattern or DAO layer.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered in controllers with no abstraction pattern. SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Implement a repository/service pattern layer. Use ActiveRecord properly with parameterized queries.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: MySQL 5.1 reached EOL in December 2013 — over a decade without security patches or vendor support.
findings.gap: Database engine is past EOL with known unpatched CVEs and no version management.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to MySQL 8.0+ on Amazon RDS with automated version management and patching.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. MySQL 5.1 on EC2 has no KMS encryption. Payment card numbers stored without encryption.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest configured for any data store. Sensitive payment data stored without encryption.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS with encryption at rest (KMS). Implement field-level encryption for PCI-sensitive data. Use tokenization.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No API authentication. OrdersController has no before_filter for authentication. Endpoints are open.
findings.gap: No API authentication — endpoints are open to unauthenticated access including order/payment data.
findings.recommendation: Implement authentication middleware. All endpoints handling sensitive data must require authentication.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. The application has no authentication at all.
findings.gap: Application has no authentication — no centralized IdP, no local auth system.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito as the centralized identity provider with OAuth2/OIDC flows.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext payment gateway credentials (merchant_id, api_password) committed to source control in config/payment.yml.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in version-controlled files. Critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate exposed credentials. Migrate all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. EC2 instances running Ruby 1.8.7 (EOL) with Mongrel (unmaintained). Known CVEs.
findings.gap: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images. Runtime has known unpatched CVEs.
findings.recommendation: Implement SSM Patch Manager. Add vulnerability scanning. Upgrade to supported Ruby/Rails versions.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No CI/CD pipeline exists at all. Known SQL injection and mass-assignment vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools — no SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No pipeline exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with SAST (Semgrep), dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk), and security gates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing — debugging failures across the application and payment gateway is guesswork.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry SDK. Propagate trace IDs through payment gateway calls.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No monitoring artifacts, no CloudWatch alarms, no latency or availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical user journeys: order placement success rate, checkout latency, payment processing success rate.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business outcome tracking.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no visibility into business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for orders_created, payments_succeeded, payments_failed, order_value.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no incident notification.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures go undetected until customers report them.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Add anomaly detection for payment failure rate.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: Tests are a stale Test::Unit suite that no longer runs. No functional test suite, no integration tests.
findings.gap: No integration tests — only a stale test suite that no longer executes. No safety net for changes.
findings.recommendation: Build a new test suite with integration tests covering critical workflows. Run in CI as quality gate.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no CODEOWNERS for observability.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is entirely absent.
findings.recommendation: Define per-service dashboards and alarms with named team owners.
